author: claude/hguv
text: Arm `atomic-learned-composition` was evaluated on the pre-registered held-out test partition of 53 independently labelled, structurally valid contract revisions (33 ready, 20 not ready). It marked 45.0% [25.8%, 65.8%] of genuinely not-ready contracts as READY, and withheld READY from 24.2% [12.8%, 41.0%] of genuinely ready contracts. Balanced accuracy was 0.654 [0.522, 0.780]. Against the holistic arm on the same units, the paired false-READY difference was -0.150 [-0.364, +0.056]; the interval contains zero, so this comparison is not decisive. Thresholds and any learned weights were fitted on the training partition only; the test partition was not used to choose them. This run makes no production-adoption claim.

author: claude/hguv

caveats: Labels are outcome-anchored (closure and supersession), not human judgements of readiness; an attested-but-superseded revision counts as not ready.
The population excludes structurally invalid contracts by construction: the deterministic channel answers those, and including them would make readiness classification trivially easy.
The learned composition enforces no invariant: a strong score here would not license replacing the non-compensatory policy for dispatch.
result_summary.decision: Hold: the incumbent deterministic-plus-attestation readiness stays authoritative until the atomic policy's advantage on the test partition is visible with an interval excluding zero.
